title: Screen Texture does not update on macOS with Chrome
body:
### Tested versions Reproducible in Godot 4.4 and 4.4.1 with Chrome and Brave, but not firefox. No issue on windows either. Brave est à jour [Version 1.77.95 Chromium: 135.0.7049.52 (Build officiel) (arm64)](https://brave.com/latest/) Mise à jour de Chrome Version 135.0.7049.41 (Build officiel) (arm64) Firefox 137 ### System information macOS Sequoia 15.3.2 Compatibility renderer ### Issue description When using a depth shader and ascreen texture (to make fog) the screen texture doesn't get updated causing it to stick and stay on the screen. Like this on a similar project ### Steps to reproduce Unzip the MRP on a mac. Export the project in the .export folder to index.html Launch the web server ``` python3 serve.py ``` Move around with the arrow keys. Notice the glitch. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19634527/mrp.zip) Discord discussion with another example:
``` Stan` — Yesterday at 12:21 PM I have a weird smearing effect if i enable the screen texture in my web export, firefox works fine, but chrome doesn't, any ideas ? Image The screen_texture doesn't get updated unless I resize the window Mao — Yesterday at 12:42 PM and how'sit supposed to look Usually I have problems with post-processing when it comes to web exports open the dev console and see if you're getting any errors in the browser Stan` — Yesterday at 12:44 PM No errors Supposed to look like this Image But it keeps the first time it was loaded Image Shader is quite simple https://termbin.com/i9x0m Mao — Yesterday at 12:48 PM The smearing effect usually means uninitialized space so your render texture is having problems not entirely sure why different browsers would impact it though Stan` — Yesterday at 12:49 PM screen_texture is sent by godot, so I have no control over it Mao — Yesterday at 12:50 PM oh, so you arent making a second viewport? Could try that Stan` — Yesterday at 12:50 PM Well the minimap is a second viewport that's a top view of the scene, yet it's displaying what's in front of me (And it should also ignore the fog alltoghether since it's not in the same visibility layer) Mao — Yesterday at 12:51 PM I mean, you can make another render texture instead of using screen_texture, assuming this is some buffer that godot creates to blit the previous frame Stan` — Yesterday at 12:52 PM If I put a black texture it's fine as in it displays stuff correcly but not what I want :D peanos — Yesterday at 12:52 PM any1 know how i can fix the bullets hitting 2+ entities at once Haskeller — Yesterday at 12:54 PM Different implementations Mao — Yesterday at 12:54 PM webgl also has limited color formats (no floating points) which could be related too, but again I'm not too sure what browsers impose onto it Stan` — Yesterday at 12:56 PM Yeah, maybe web export don't support screen_textures on chrome, but I find it hard to believe Mao — Yesterday at 12:57 PM I tried doing a full-screen distortion shader for a project and maybe I ran into a similar problem Stan` — Yesterday at 12:57 PM I also could not find an open issue about it, but I don't know the technical terms, smearing sounds close Mao — Yesterday at 12:58 PM it's just non-rendered space, similar to not rendering a skybox so what's happening is it's not being cleared every frame Stan` — Yesterday at 12:59 PM Yeah it keeps the same screen_texture forever Mao — Yesterday at 12:59 PM I'd try your own render texture and see if that does anything usually have a few more properties you can play with on it Stan` — Yesterday at 1:01 PM I don't know if I can get the screen texture from anywhere it's bound through the hint Mao — Yesterday at 1:03 PM ignore it. Make your own text2D buffer and send in the render texture and sample that Stan` — Yesterday at 1:05 PM Sure, but make it from what ? Where would I get the screen's pixels ? Mao — Yesterday at 1:06 PM subviewport You know what. It could also be the depth texture being a problem, but I would expect you to get errors in the dev console about it Stan` — Yesterday at 1:17 PM I switched to subviewport and it's the same so maybe It's working fine in firefox tho Mmmh I do get this with the subviewport now localhost/:1 [.WebGL-0x11000a45600] GL_INVALID_OPERATION: Feedback loop formed between Framebuffer and active Texture. Aedda [4.3] — Yesterday at 1:20 PM String.replace is confusing me... specifically the second parameter forwhat is that supposed to be format? I thought at first it was fromwhat meaning the source string but the syntax for it is already fromwhat.replace(what...??
